top.headline: Front knee collapses to 159 deg at release
top.title: Brace the front leg

metrics.label: Back-foot to front-foot contact
metrics.explain: Duration of the delivery stride. Reported +/- one frame (40 ms for this footage).

metrics.label: Front-foot contact to release
metrics.explain: How quickly you go from landing to letting the ball go. Shorter (with a stable front leg) usually means better energy transfer.

metrics.label: Elbow extension (UAH -> release)
metrics.note: Elbow extension needs 120-240 fps slow motion (this clip has ~25 distinct fps); it isn't estimated from this video. Never a substitute for an accredited ICC test.
metrics.norm: Legal bowlers: 0-10 deg (mean ~6 deg); ICC limit 15 deg
metrics.ref: ICC Illegal Bowling Regulations; Ferdinands & Kersting 2005; King & Yeadon 2013
metrics.explain: Straightening of the bowling elbow between the arm passing horizontal and release, computed the ICC way (maximum flexion minus the following minimum). A single camera cannot replace an accredited ICC test - use this only as a screening estimate.

metrics.label: Front knee at release
metrics.norm: Elite men 167 +/- 19 deg at release; straighter knee correlates with ball speed (r~0.4)
metrics.explain: A straighter front leg at release acts as a lever and is associated with higher ball speed; some flexion is normal and may reduce load.

metrics.label: Front knee collapse after landing
metrics.norm: Elite men flex 9 +/- 11 deg after FFC (heuristic band)
metrics.explain: Flexion of the front knee from landing to its most bent point. Together with the extension to release it gives the front-leg technique (Portus et al. 2004).

metrics.label: Back knee at back-foot contact
metrics.norm: Injured bowlers 146 deg vs uninjured 156 deg at BFC (rear hip/knee)
metrics.explain: A very flexed back leg at back-foot contact was one of the strongest predictors of lumbar stress injury in a prospective elite study.

metrics.label: Trunk forward flexion at release
metrics.norm: Elite men ~42 +/- 5 deg forward at release (heuristic band)
metrics.explain: How far the trunk is pitched towards the batter at release. Fast bowlers flex strongly through the delivery stride.

metrics.label: Trunk flexion FFC -> release
metrics.norm: Elite men flex the trunk 31 +/- 8 deg from FFC to release
metrics.explain: Trunk flexion produced during the delivery stride - a key contributor to ball speed.

metrics.label: Trunk side-bend at release
metrics.note: Not measurable from this camera view - film behind the bowler or front-on to measure it.
metrics.norm: Later-injured juniors 50 +/- 6 deg vs uninjured 40 +/- 8 deg (thorax lateral flexion at BR)
metrics.ref: Bayne et al. 2016; contested in elite adults (Alway 2021)
metrics.explain: Lateral flexion of the trunk away from the bowling arm. Large side-bend loads the lower back; it is one of the better single-camera measures from behind the bowler.

metrics.label: Shoulder alignment at back-foot contact
metrics.note: Not measurable from this camera view - film behind the bowler or front-on to measure it.

metrics.label: Hip-shoulder separation at BFC
metrics.note: Not measurable from this camera view - film behind the bowler or front-on to measure it.
metrics.norm: >= 30 deg at BFC classifies a mixed action
metrics.explain: Misalignment between hips and shoulders when the back foot lands; large values define a 'mixed' action, which twists the lower back.

metrics.label: Shoulder counter-rotation
metrics.note: Not measurable from this camera view - film behind the bowler or front-on to measure it.
metrics.norm: >= 30 deg is the common mixed-action criterion (stronger evidence in juniors)
metrics.explain: How much the shoulders rotate back towards side-on after back-foot contact.

metrics.label: Release height
metrics.norm: Elite men 113 +/- 4 % of standing height (heuristic band)
metrics.explain: Height of the ball at release as a percentage of your height (~1.75 m for a stature of 1.80 m). Single-camera precision is about +/- 8 points.

metrics.label: Arm slot at release
metrics.note: Not measurable from this camera view - film behind the bowler or front-on to measure it.
metrics.norm: Angle of the bowling arm from vertical at release (descriptive; higher slot often costs more side-bend)
metrics.explain: 0 deg = bowling arm straight up (high arm); larger = more round-arm.

metrics.label: Delivery stride length
metrics.norm: Elite men 79 +/- 7 % of standing height (heuristic band)
metrics.explain: Distance between the ankles at front-foot contact.

priorities.headline: Front knee collapses to 159 deg at release
priorities.why: A straighter front leg at release acts as a lever and is associated with higher ball speed; some flexion is normal and may reduce load.

drill.title: Brace the front leg
drill.cue: Land tall, push the ground away - 'stand up' through the front leg as the arm comes over.
drills: Standing brace: front foot planted, bowl from a static delivery-stride position, focus on a firm knee (3 x 6).
Walk-through then jog-through deliveries, adding speed only while the knee stays firm (3 x 6).
Gather-and-bound drill onto a mat, freezing at front-foot contact to feel the brace (2 x 8).

priorities.headline: Upright trunk at release (20 deg)
priorities.why: How far the trunk is pitched towards the batter at release. Fast bowlers flex strongly through the delivery stride.

drill.title: Drive the chest through
drill.cue: Chest over the front knee - finish with your bowling shoulder pointing at the batter.
drills: Kneeling throws: front knee down, pull the trunk down and through towards a target (3 x 8).
Med-ball slam from the delivery stride position (17+ only) (3 x 6).
Follow-through line drill: finish with the chest past the front knee on a chalk line (2 x 8).

priorities.headline: Release point is low (97% of height)
priorities.why: Height of the ball at release as a percentage of your height (~1.75 m for a stature of 1.80 m). Single-camera precision is about +/- 8 points.

drill.title: Get taller at release
drill.cue: Tall at the crease - bowling arm brushes the ear, release at the top.
drills: High-target drill: release over a raised rope/bar 1 m in front of the crease (3 x 6).
Standing-start bowling focusing on reaching up through the bowling arm (3 x 6).

all_issues.headline: Short delivery stride (53% of height; typical 70-87%)
all_issues.why: Distance between the ankles at front-foot contact.

drill.title: Find your stride
drill.cue: Bound up, not along - land with a stride that lets you stay tall.
drills: Stride markers: mark a target front-foot position at ~75-80% of your height from the back foot (3 x 6).
Bound and stick: bound into the delivery stride and hold balance for two seconds (2 x 8).

strengths: Firm back leg at back-foot contact
Good trunk flexion through the crease
capture_tips: Filmed at 25 fps - the arm moves ~80 deg between frames at release. Use 120-240 fps slow motion for precise release and elbow measurements.
Filmed side-on: knee, trunk flexion, stride and release height are measured well; add a clip from behind the bowler for side-bend and alignment.
coaching.disclaimer: Estimates from a single video. Not a medical assessment and not an ICC legality test.
